title: Cassandra Quick Guide
description: Find a short explanation and a worked example for each idea in the Cassandra course.

entries.name: Create a local practice keyspace
entries.summary: A keyspace groups Cassandra tables and defines replication.

example.code:
CREATE KEYSPACE IF NOT EXISTS cma_reading WITH replication = {'class':'SimpleStrategy','replication_factor':1};
USE cma_reading;

entries.name: Design a table for one question
entries.summary: The partition key chooses a group of rows stored together.

example.code: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS reading_by_reader(reader_id text,day date,title text,pages int,PRIMARY KEY((reader_id),day)) WITH CLUSTERING ORDER BY(day DESC);

entries.name: Insert a reading entry
entries.summary: An INSERT writes values at a primary-key address.

entries.name: Read one partition
entries.summary: A Cassandra query is efficient when it names the partition key.

example.code: SELECT day,title,pages FROM reading_by_reader WHERE reader_id='mia';

entries.name: Read a range inside a partition
entries.summary: After choosing a partition, a query can use a range on its clustering column.

example.code: SELECT day,title FROM reading_by_reader WHERE reader_id='mia' AND day>='2026-11-01' LIMIT 5;

entries.name: Keep partitions a manageable size
entries.summary: A partition should not grow without a useful bound.

example.code: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS reading_by_month(reader_id text,month text,day date,title text,PRIMARY KEY((reader_id,month),day));

entries.name: Expire temporary fields
entries.summary: A TTL gives written values a time to live.

example.code:
INSERT INTO reading_by_reader(reader_id,day,title,pages) VALUES('temporary-reader','2026-11-16','Practice',1) USING TTL 60;
SELECT TTL(title) FROM reading_by_reader WHERE reader_id='temporary-reader' AND day='2026-11-16';

entries.name: Update by the full key
entries.summary: An UPDATE names the row through its key and changes selected values.

example.code: UPDATE reading_by_reader SET pages=25 WHERE reader_id='mia' AND day='2026-11-16';

entries.name: Delete one known row
entries.summary: A DELETE marks selected data as deleted.

example.code: DELETE FROM reading_by_reader WHERE reader_id='temporary-reader' AND day='2026-11-16';

entries.name: Group a small related write
entries.summary: A batch can group related mutations. It is not a general speed trick for sending many unrelated partitions at once.

entries.name: Use a dedicated counter table
entries.summary: Cassandra counters use a special column type and update rules.

entries.name: Match consistency to the cluster
entries.summary: A consistency level tells Cassandra how many replicas must answer an operation.

example.code:
Worked example with three replicas:
ONE needs one replica response.
QUORUM needs a majority: two responses.
The local course has only one replica, so it cannot demonstrate surviving multiple replica failures.
